jobs.title: Software Development Engineer, Amazon Marketing Cloud Assistant
jobs.description: Application deadline: Nov 14, 2026 Build the AI-powered conversational agent that's transforming how advertisers interact with their data—replacing SQL queries and complex UIs with natural language that simply works. You'll work at the intersection of large language models, distributed systems, and petabyte-scale advertising data, shipping a high-visibility product at the forefront of generative AI in advertising. We're looking for a Software Development Engineer II who is excited to solve hard, novel problems: natural language understanding, data accuracy at scale, agent evaluation, and translating complex analytical workflows into intuitive AI-driven experiences. In this role, you will: - Design and build core backend services powering an LLM-based conversational assistant for Amazon Marketing Cloud - Own end-to-end delivery of features—from system design through production deployment and operational excellence - Build scalable data pipelines and infrastructure that ingest and process petabyte-scale advertising data from multiple sources - Shape the future of how advertisers generate insights, build audiences, and optimize campaigns through AI This is a fast-paced, ownership-driven environment where you'll collaborate across science, product, and engineering to ship products that directly impact how millions of advertisers succeed on Amazon. Who We're Looking For We seek someone with a strong coding foundation and experience building distributed systems at scale—someone energized by ambiguity and fast-moving problem spaces. Ideal candidates bring curiosity about LLM-based applications and a track record of delivering customer-facing products end to end. Experience with advertising technology, analytics platforms, or AWS services is a plus. Key job responsibilities AI Assistant Platform - Design, develop, and maintain backend services powering the AMC conversational assistant - Build and optimize LLM orchestration pipelines including prompt engineering, tool use, and agent workflows - Develop APIs and integrations with AMC's query engine, reporting services, and audience management systems - Collaborate with applied scientists to integrate ML models and improve response quality - Contribute to the evaluation framework—designing metrics, building ground truth datasets, and improving agent accuracy Data Infrastructure - Implement and maintain scalable data pipelines to ingest, process, and store petabyte-scale log-level advertising data from multiple sources (ad servers, exchanges, SSPs) - Build ETL workflows that transform raw event-level data into queryable, analysis-ready formats following established architectural patterns - Create and maintain APIs that enable analytics teams and data scientists to query log-level data efficiently - Implement data quality checks, validation logic, and monitoring for data pipelines and services - Optimize performance and cost efficiency of data processing jobs and queries Engineering Excellence - Own end-to-end delivery of features from design through production deployment - Write clean, well-tested code and participate in code reviews to maintain high engineering standards - Improve system reliability, latency, and scalability as the product scales to more advertisers - Debug and resolve production issues, participating in on-call rotations as needed - Document systems, processes, and runbooks to support operational excellence - Collaborate with senior engineers to contribute to design discussions and architectural decisions About the team The Amazon Marketing Cloud (AMC) Assistant team is building an AI-powered conversational agent that helps advertisers interact with AMC through natural language. jobs.title: Software Development Engineer, AIO Visualization and Reporting
jobs.description: Join a team that builds the experiences every AWS customer uses to understand, monitor, and optimize what they spend, from individual developers to enterprise FinOps teams managing tens of millions of dollars in monthly spend. The AWS Billing Console Platform team owns the console's hosting platform, on which around thirty AWS engineering teams build their console pages; over fifty customer-facing billing and cost pages of its own; and the rendering engine that turns an AI agent's cost data into the charts, tables and reports customers see. Two AWS agents answer cost questions today, a FinOps agent and Amazon Q in the console, and chatbots and console pages form one ecosystem customers navigate between to get problems solved and questions answered. Today each renders its answers its own way, and a cost figure has to be right the first time. This team is building the rendering layer both agents will draw on: an engine that checks every plotted value against the data the agent gathered, an open artifact format any agent host can render, and the component catalog that makes a cost chart look the same wherever it appears. We are hiring a Software Development Engineer to extend this rendering platform to provide effective visualization for any problem that our web pages handle, especially for risky mutative actions. You'll use only the latest genAI, open source and proprietary technologies to directly enhance agents to give them the power of our AWS management console pages for problems that can only be solved visually or that require supervision by users. Key job responsibilities - Design, build, test, and operate the rendering engine behind AWS's cost agents: the components, the emit path, and the checks that verify every number before a customer sees it. - Bring generated cost visualizations into agent conversations against the accuracy and customer-outcome bars the team sets, and keep two agent hosts rendering the same artifact from the same data. - Define and publish a rendering format for cost artifacts and adopt the open protocol the console ecosystem is converging on. - Build and operate customer-facing console pages on the team's page-building platform and component library. - Help scale a platform that absorbed the work of three teams in a 2026 reorganization: drive down operational load through automation, observability, and legacy-service decommissioning so the team can invest in new customer experiences. - Own services end to end, including participation in the team's on-call rotation for production support. - Raise engineering quality through design reviews, code reviews, automated evaluation, and operational excellence, and partner with product managers, applied scientists, designers, and the agent teams across AWS. A day in the life You start by checking the health of the services you own and clearing anything handed off from on-call, then pick up your current project: maybe a new artifact type, where you run the agent's answers through the team's fidelity scorecard, read where a figure drifted from its source, and fix the emit path. Midday you review a teammate's component, then join a design review where the team and the agent teams weigh how one artifact renders in two hosts. In the afternoon you pair with an applied scientist on the evaluation set for the next release and sketch the components a new chart needs. Across the week you balance net-new rendering and platform work against the operational excellence that billing customers depend on, and rotate through on-call. The problems are open-ended, the customer scale is large, and the design space is new, so there is room to set technical direction and take on new scope. You will have the support of an experienced team and a manager invested in your growth. About the team The AWS Billing Console Platform team owns the platform, the customer-facing pages, and the rendering engine that AWS customers and AWS's cost agents use to manage cloud spend. We operate at scale. Around thirty AWS engineering teams build their console pages on our hosting platform, which gains two to three new console pages every year, and we own over fifty customer-facing pages ourselves, with a production footprint consolidated from three teams in a 2026 reorganization and driven toward lower operational load through automation and legacy-service decommissioning. We own generative UI for billing and cost management, the rendering engine the FinOps agent runs in production and the cost-visualization skill Amazon Q is launching, and we are extending that ownership into a platform: the agent interfaces, the generated experiences, and the open format customers will see across AWS's cost agents. That combination, a large operational platform plus a green-field AI mandate, means an engineer here can take on scope quickly and see a clear path to the next level. We operate what we build, hold a high bar for operational excellence, and care about inclusion, mentorship, and work-life harmony, so engineers at every level can do their best work and grow their careers. - 3+ years of non-internship professional software development experience - 2+ years of non-internship design or architecture (design patterns, reliability and scaling) of new and existing systems experience - 1+ years of software development engineer or related occupational experience - 1+ years of designing and developing large-scale, multi-tiered, multi-threaded, embedded or distributed software applications, tools, systems, and services using: C#, C++, Java, or Perl experience - 1+ years of Object Oriented Design experience - Bachelor's degree or foreign equivalent in Computer Science, Engineering, Mathematics, or a related field - Experience programming with at least one software programming language - 3+ years of full software development life cycle, including coding standards, code reviews, source control management, build processes, testing, and operations experience - Bachelor's degree in computer science or equivalent Amazon is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of protected veteran status, disability, or other legally protected status. jobs.title: Software Engineer, Worldwide Amazon Stores Finance Technology, Controllership Engineering
jobs.description: Amazon's finance teams rely on financial controls to keep spending accurate and financial reports audit-ready. You will build the systems that automate those controls, catch errors and waste before money is spent, and give finance analysts fast, trusted answers through AI tools built on cloud services and large-scale data. Key job responsibilities - Build services that check purchase requests and orders against finance rules in near real time, then correct or flag issues before approval. - Automate financial controls, such as reviews of fixed assets, leases, cost centers, open orders, so finance teams spend less time collecting data by hand and more time acting on exceptions. - Build data pipelines on AWS, including Lambda, StepFunctions, Glue, EMR, DDB, and S3, that feed C-Hub/dashboards finance teams use during month-end close and audit reviews. - Build AI agents on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore with the Strands SDK, including MCP tools, context and memory management, evaluation, harnesses, and guardrails that keep finance answers accurate. - Big data experience with Spark, StarRocks, or similar OLAP engines. - Build web applications and browser extensions in React and TypeScript that let finance users review exceptions, filter large datasets, and export results. - Turn defined business requirements into technical designs, review them with senior engineers, and take them from prototype to production. - Own your services in production. Write the tests, alarms, and automated rollbacks that let a change reach customers in hours, not days. Take part in on-call rotation. - Work directly with finance, accounting, product, and data science partners, and explain technical tradeoffs. A day in the life Most of your day goes to building. You might start by looking into an alarm from an overnight data job that feeds a finance control. Then you meet an accounting partner to design how a manual review could run automatically. After lunch, you write code and tests and ship the change through an automated pipeline the same day. Some weeks, you test a new AI model against an evaluation set to see if it gives better answers. Near month-end close, you answer finance users who want to know why a control flagged a transaction. About the team We are a team of software engineers who build the tools that keep Amazon's spending accurate and its financial reports audit-ready. Our customers are finance analysts, accountants, and employees across Amazon who buy goods and services. We own our products end to end, from data pipelines and services to the web apps and AI agents people use every day. We ship changes through automated pipelines and measure our work by the manual effort and errors we remove. We value clear writing, careful reviews, and engineers who ask why a process exists before they automate it. - 3+ years of non-internship professional software development experience - 2+ years of non-internship design or architecture (design patterns, reliability and scaling) of new and existing systems experience - Experience programming with at least one software programming language - Bachelor's degree or equivalent - 3+ years of full software development life cycle, including coding standards, code reviews, source control management, build processes, testing, and operations experience - Knowledge of machine learning model architecture and inference - Knowledge of computer architecture, operating systems, and parallel computing - Knowledge of professional software engineering & best practices for full software development life cycle, including coding standards, software architectures, code reviews, source control management, continuous deployments, testing, and operational excellence Amazon is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of protected veteran status, disability, or other legally protected status. jobs.title: Software Development Engineer, AWS Route 53, AWS Route 53 Frontier Resolver
jobs.description: AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re looking for talented people who want to help. You’ll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You’ll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. And you’ll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion. AWS Route 53 Resolver team has an open position for Software Development Engineer for Cloud security service development in Arlington, VA / Herndon, VA / Seattle, WA, USA. We’re looking for a mid-level Software Development Engineer to join the Amazon Route 53 Frontier Resolver team. Our team builds and operates a globally distributed DNS resolution service that enables AWS customers to securely resolve internal and external DNS names across regions, networks, and hybrid environments. You will help ensure that DNS queries are resolved securely, reliably, and within milliseconds for enterprise customers running workloads across VPCs, on-prem, and edge locations. As an SDE, This is a rare opportunity to build a new AWS service from its preview launch toward global scale. You will work across the entire stack—control plane, data plane, API surfaces, and deep integrations with AGA, EC2 Networking, DNS Firewall, and Route 53 core systems. You will also help drive the system architecture, spearhead best practices that enable a quality product, and help coach and develop junior engineers. A successful candidate will have an established background in engineering large scale networking software, great communication skills, and a motivation to achieve results in a fast paced environment. At Amazon Web Services, we like to “work backwards”: start by understanding what customers need and using that to guide our software engineering. We’re looking for a software engineer who is experienced in listening to customers, synthesizing their needs, and rapidly iterating our services to quickly put features into customers’ hands. Our best ideas become even better when we get feedback from real customer use. The sooner we can get that feedback, the more quickly we can grow. This position will be part of the Amazon Route 53 team. Amazon Route 53 is a highly available and scalable Domain Name System (DNS) service offered by Amazon Web Services. We operate in over 50 locations worldwide and provide advanced functionality such as Private DNS, DNS Firewall, DNS resolver and integration with a plethora of AWS services. On top of that, we offer fast change propagation with a 100% availability SLA. Our service is quickly growing and we're expanding in multiple directions: adding new features and functionality to our DNS services, better traffic management, new AWS integrations, improving our health check capabilities, and expanding with new security services and routing space. We work on deep, technical problems that span a variety of core topics in computer science ranging from databases to networking to distributed systems to numerical analysis to security. We are looking for a developer who will lead the team and who feels strongly not only about building good software but also about running that software in the real world. Amazon in a fast-paced environment where we “Work Hard, Have Fun, Make History.” On a typical day, software engineers might whip up a prototype to prove an idea, instrument code to report a new metric, talk with customers, code up a feature, or draft a proposal for a radical new idea. jobs.description: We see our customers as invited guests to a party, and we are the hosts. It's our job every day to make every important aspect of the customer experience a little bit better." - Jeff Bezos, Founder & CEO We didn’t make Amazon a trillion-dollar company, our customers did, and we want to ensure that our customers always have a positive experience that keeps them coming back to Amazon. To help achieve this, the Customer Experience Improvement (CXI) team, within Amazon Customer Service (CS), relentlessly focuses on maintaining customer trust by building products that offer appropriate resolutions to resolve issues faced by our customers. CXI engineers solve complex problems and build scalable, robust solutions to help our customers navigate through issues and eliminate systemic defects to prevent future issues and identify critical customer experience improvement opportunities. This role will leverage latest technologies and Agentic AI solutions to autonomously eliminate defects at scale to improve customer experience. Key job responsibilities - Design, develop, and own scalable solutions that empower Amazon to deliver a defect-free experience for customers. - Build intuitive tools for Customer Service Associates (CSAs) to escalate critical issues, and develop complex integrations with Tier-1 Amazon systems and advanced science models to detect, triage, and resolve systemic defects. - Tackle complex technical challenges, create innovative solutions with direct impact on customer trust, and work on systems critical to Amazon's operational excellence. About the team ARCADE (Automated Root Causing, Attribution and Defect Elimination) is the Defect Elimination system within CXI Tech, manifesting Amazon's commitment to preventing customers from receiving defective products that degrade their experience. ARCADE leverages AI to transform how we detect repeat negative customer experiences and eliminate the underlying upstream defects at scale. The CXI Tech team re-imagines how we leverage customer interactions and feedback — through modular capabilities spanning Detection, Triage, Root Cause, Attribution, and Resolution — to enable more reliable and faster defect elimination that drives customer experience improvements throughout the consumer business. The system combines associate-driven signals (empowering front-line CSAs to flag product problems) with statistical and machine learning-based automated detection, intelligent prioritization, and increasingly autonomous investigation through our agentic ecosystem.
